summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining GPT-backed language models, arithmetic reasoning, and code generation to solve multi-step mathematical problems. By utilizing error-driven prompt optimization and constraint-guided frameworks, models convert erroneous predictions into structured optimization signals to improve execution accuracy. The approach leverages open-source repositories and packages such as repo:qwenlm/qwen3 and pkg:skythought to build robust reasoning workflows.

target_user.text: The target users are software developers and quantitative analysts working with on-premises small language models and code generation agents, as inferred from repository tooling and package distribution patterns in the bundle.

jtbd.text: Perform accurate multi-step arithmetic operations on structured data while ensuring sensitive information remains secure in on-premises environments.

value_prop.text: Enables reliable, interpretable, and industrially deployable AI assistants that achieve high arithmetic accuracy through systematic, error-driven prompt optimization and constraint-guided planning rather than costly fine-tuning.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is on axis V (viability), which was designated due to missing evidence in the bundle. We assume that enterprise customers will pay for an on-premises GPT-backed code generation agent for arithmetic reasoning workflows.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with enterprise data analysts to evaluate willingness to pay for a secure, on-premises arithmetic code generation agent.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: A proposed threshold of 40 percent of interviewed enterprise stakeholders confirm a willingness to purchase or pilot the solution at a proposed threshold price of 500 dollars per month.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of interviewed enterprise stakeholders express willingness to pay for the proposed solution.

open_source.use: Serves as the underlying foundational large language model series for on-premises deployment.
Provides reasoning capabilities to support structured multi-step planning and thought tracing.

to_build.text: An error-driven prompt optimization module that clusters erroneous predictions to iteratively refine prompt rules for code generation agents.
A constraint-guided search framework utilizing intent-constraint pairs to ensure generated plans satisfy symbolic rules.
